customer_acct: Hi — we're seeing intermittent 503s when our service in a VPC talks to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate through our corporate HTTP proxy. It succeeds for a while then fails with 503 'upstream reset'. Direct egress to internet works fine. Anyone seen this pattern with CONNECT tunnels?
maria-support: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste a minimal curl repro + whether your proxy is doing TLS inspection (MITM)? Also any Agent logs you can share (redact tokens).
customer_acct: Repro with curl (we used a throwaway token):
```
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 --proxytunnel \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer TEST_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Auth: acct-123" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
It sometimes returns a 503 body 'upstream reset' right after headers, sometimes works. Our infra team confirmed the proxy does TLS inspection / re-signs certs.
kevin-eng: TLS inspection + CONNECT is a common cause. If the proxy terminates TLS, it can rewrite SNI/Host and strip custom headers. Can you capture a pcap of the ClientHello so we can confirm SNI? Example tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s0 -w /tmp/cap.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host api.redwood.ai'`
jordan-priv-deploy: From our edge logs we see a lot of requests whose Host header is `internal-corp-gw` and the X-Redwood-Auth header is missing for the failing calls. That would cause our auth middleware to reject or for upstream to reset. Also saw several connections where the proxy responds with an HTTP payload mid-tunnel, then FINs.
sre-oncall: Can you also run a verbose curl that shows the proxy exchange? `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 --proxytunnel https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer TEST_TOKEN'` — capture the full output. If the proxy injects an extra HTTP/1.1 response before the TLS stream, that'll break the handshake and produce the errors you describe.
customer_acct: We ran tcpdump and grepped the ClientHello — the SNI is often `corp-inspect.example` not `api.redwood.ai`. That matches the MITM cert we see in the browser. We can upload pcap.
maria-support: That confirms TLS MITM. Two likely routes: (A) Have your security team configure the proxy to allow TLS passthrough for `api.redwood.ai` (no inspection), or (B) preserve SNI/Host and custom headers when proxying (some proxies can be configured to forward Host and not strip headers). Which of those is feasible?
customer_acct: Security says inspection is required for most traffic but they can create an allowlist for certain vendor endpoints. They asked if Redwood has static IP ranges we can allowlist instead of domain-based rules.
kevin-eng: We publish Dedicated/edge IP ranges for allowlisting. Short-term workaround: if you can whitelist our egress IPs (we'll provide the list) the proxy can be configured to do passthrough for that CIDR. Long-term: consider reworking auth to not rely on custom proxy-mutable headers — e.g., standard Authorization bearer tokens over TLS (which you're already doing), or mTLS so MITM can't impersonate client.
infra-bot: automated: service-edge spike: 2026-03-01T10:22:00Z — 502/503 rate increased 7x for traffic from corp-networks. Correlates with connection resets from proxy inspection.
sre-oncall: Also check proxy idle/timeout settings — some proxies send premature RSTs on long-lived streaming connections. If you're using streaming responses (server-sent tokens), proxy timeouts can close the tunnel and trigger upstream resets. Ask netops to increase CONNECT idle time or disable intermediate buffering for those endpoints.
customer_acct: We reproduced with the verbose curl. Output shows `HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established` then 1-2s of data then `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with a body from the proxy before TLS finishes — looks like content inspection injecting something.
maria-support: Okay next steps: 1) Please upload the pcap + redacted curl verbose output to the secure link I DMed you. 2) Ask your proxy team to either: a) configure passthrough for api.redwood.ai or our published IP ranges, OR b) ensure the proxy does NOT rewrite SNI/Host and preserves headers for CONNECT tunnels to our host. 3) If inspection cannot be relaxed, request a specific rule to allow direct egress to our Dedicated IPs.
kevin-eng: For your network team, useful checks: tcpdump of ClientHello to verify SNI, look for re-signed cert CN that belongs to corp inspect device, check proxy ACLs for `tunneled` vs `intercept` modes, and capture proxy logs showing CONNECT handling. Example tcpdump filter to capture TLS handshakes: `tcpdump -i any -n -s0 -vvv 'tcp port 443 and host api.redwood.ai' -w /tmp/443.pcap`
jordan-priv-deploy: We'll prepare the IP ranges and a short explainer your netops can quote to support ticket them. Also note: if your app relies on custom in-flight headers (like X-Redwood-Auth) those are fragile when inspection is present.
customer_acct: Thanks — uploading artifacts now. tagging @security-team in the ticket. Appreciate fast triage. :thumbsup:
maria-support: Thanks — setting P0. We'll keep you updated once we have netops response or after reviewing pcap.
